summary: In this story, a usually noisy class must work in total silence during a reading exercise, and one boy who struggles to focus discovers he actually reads better in a quiet room.
introduce: Show the title “The Day the Classroom Went Quiet” and ask, “What do you think will happen in this story, and why?” Explain that good readers use clues in the text together with what they already know to make inferences.

keyTerms.def: to focus your mind completely on one task
something that takes your attention away from a task
the usual order of things someone does regularly

challengeTerms.def: to involve yourself completely in an activity or situation
able to do or make a useful amount of work
a clear understanding of something, often gained suddenly

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that classrooms should always be lively, with lots of talking and discussion, instead of quiet? Use evidence from the story to explain.
Explain how Faisal's experience during the silent reading time changed what he understood about himself.
struggling: Read the first part of the story aloud together, review concentrate, distraction, and routine, and let weak readers answer “What clue tells you that?” questions using sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use immerse, productive, and insight in a short paragraph that makes an inference that the story does not state and support it with two clues.
